filename: Integrating Scientific Knowledge with Machine Learning for Engineering and Environmental Systems.pdf
title: Integrating Scientific Knowledge with Machine Learning for Engineering and Environmental Systems
testbed_rationale: This is a survey and review paper synthesizing physics-guided machine learning methods across engineering and environmental systems; no new datasets or benchmarks are created or distributed.
pain_points: High labeled data requirements for black-box ML models in scientific domains
Physical inconsistency of standard ML predictions violating conservation laws
Poor out-of-sample generalization to unseen regimes
Prohibitive computational expense of high-resolution mechanistic simulations and traditional PDE solvers
Ill-posedness and high computational complexity in inverse modeling
Difficult scalability of Gaussian processes and Bayesian neural networks for uncertainty quantification in high dimensions
extraction_notes: The paper is a broad review and taxonomy covering physics-guided loss functions, initializations, architectures, and hybrid models. No primary simulation or observational dataset is produced or directly trained on within the manuscript itself.
